name: Wheat
reason: Ideal for Rabi season; thrives in cool weather and fertile loamy soil.
guideSteps: Seed Selection: Prefer HD 2967, WH 1105, DBW-327, or SMW 5174. Treat seeds with Carbendazim 2.5 g/kg.
Land Prep: Prepare a fine seedbed with 2-3 ploughings. Irrigate prior to sowing if soil is dry.
Sowing: Drill seeds at 4-5 cm depth with 22 cm row spacing, using 100-125 kg/ha.
Fertilizers: Apply DAP 100 kg/ha and Potash 50 kg/ha at sowing, then topdress Urea.
Irrigation: Focus on critical watering stages: Crown Root Initiation (CRI), tillering, flowering, and grain-fill.
Harvest: Cut the crop in March-April when stalks turn golden-yellow and grains are hard.

name: Rice
reason: Great for monsoon season; requires high water and heavy alluvial/clayey soils.
guideSteps: Seed Selection: Use IR8, Sonalika, Basmati 370, or Pusa 1121. Treat with Carbendazim.
Nursery: Raise seedlings for 25-30 days while preparing puddled main field with standing water.
Transplantation: Transplant seedlings in rows with 20 cm spacing to ensure airflow.
Fertility: Apply NPK 120:60:40 kg/ha and Zinc Sulfate 25 kg/ha. Split Nitrogen applications.
Watering: Maintain 5 cm standing water until grains ripen; drain 10-12 days before harvest.
Harvesting: Reclaim grains when golden and moisture content reaches 18-20%.

name: Maize
reason: Requires well-drained fertile soils and warm monsoon weather.
guideSteps: Seed Choice: Pick Pioneer 3302, Dekalb 9108, or Syngenta NK6240 hybrid seeds.
Sowing: Spacing at 60 cm x 20 cm at 3-5 cm depth in well-tilled soil.
Fertility: Split Urea into three applications (basal, knee-high, and pre-tasseling).
Pest Alert: Scan for Fall Armyworm regularly. Apply Bacillus thuringiensis if damage is seen.
Irrigation: Keep field moist during critical knee-high and silking phases.
Harvest: Harvest when cob sheaths dry to brown and kernels become hard.

name: Barley
reason: Strong Rabi option for lighter soils and lower irrigation needs.
guideSteps: Preparation: Plow 2-3 times to prepare a clean, fine weed-free seedbed.
Sowing: Sow seeds at 22 cm row spacing and 4-5 cm depth using a seed drill.
Irrigation: Give only 2-3 waterings. Focus on tillering and booting stages.
Weed Control: Spray Pendimethalin 3 days post-sowing to suppress early winter weeds.
Harvesting: Reap when stems are dry and straw turns brittle-yellow.

name: Bajra
reason: Highly suitable for dry regions with sandy soils and low rainfall.
guideSteps: Variety selection: Use drought-resistant hybrid bajra seeds (e.g. HHB 67, MH 179).
Sowing: Direct sow at a shallow depth of 2 cm. Spacing should be 45 cm x 15 cm.
Weeding: Hoeing and weeding at 20-25 days after sowing is critical.
Watering: Can be grown rainfed; provide supplemental watering at flowering if rain fails.
Harvest: Harvest when grain moisture falls below 20% and seed heads dry out.

name: Jowar (Sorghum)
reason: Excellent drought-tolerant crop suitable for black cotton and clay loam soils.
guideSteps: Varieties: Pick CSH-14 or CSV-15 and treat seeds to avoid grain mold and shoot fly.
Soil: Prepare land well. Clayey or black soils are ideal as they retain moisture.
Sowing: Space rows at 45 cm. Maintain plant-to-plant distance at 12-15 cm.
Harvest: Cut the panicles when the grains have hardened and show a black spot at the base.

name: Ragi (Finger Millet)
reason: Highly nutritious millet; extremely hardy in red laterite and sandy soils.
guideSteps: Preparation: Sow in nursery or direct sow. Transplanting gives higher yields.
Nutrition: Apply FYM (Farm Yard Manure) at 4 tonnes/acre during field preparation.
Weeding: Hand-weed twice at 20 and 40 days to keep the crop clean.
Harvest: Harvest in two stages. First cut the earheads, then cut the stalks.
